headline: Police officer sent on compulsory retirement over relationship with Pori Moni
summary: Additional SP Golam Saklain Shithil was removed from service after a departmental case found his relationship with the actress damaged the government's image.
details: Additional Superintendent of Police Golam Saklain Shithil has been sent into compulsory retirement by the home ministry on Thursday.
The action follows allegations regarding his relationship with film actress Pori Moni, which began while he was investigating a case she filed in June 2021.
At the time, Saklain was serving as an assistant commissioner of police in the Gulshan division of the Detective Branch (DB) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police.
The home ministry stated that Saklain developed an "ethically inappropriate close relationship" with the actress outside the scope of his official duties.
Reports of an alleged extramarital relationship, including celebrating birthdays and spending time at his official residence, were cited as having "damaged the image of the government".
A departmental case was initiated against him on February 20, 2023, under the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules on charges of misconduct.
caption:
A high-ranking police officer has been forced into retirement after an "ethically inappropriate" relationship with a film star.

Additional Superintendent of Police Golam Saklain Shithil has been sent into compulsory retirement by the home ministry on Thursday.

The action follows allegations regarding his relationship with film actress Pori Moni, which began while he was investigating a case she filed in June 2021.

At the time, Saklain was serving as an assistant commissioner of police in the Gulshan division of the Detective Branch (DB) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police.

The home ministry stated that Saklain developed an "ethically inappropriate close relationship" with the actress outside the scope of his official duties.

Reports of an alleged extramarital relationship, including celebrating birthdays and spending time at his official residence, were cited as having "damaged the image of the government".

A departmental case was initiated against him on February 20, 2023, under the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules on charges of misconduct.

Source: bdnews24.com, Somoy News, Dhaka Tribune

headline_marked: [[SSC results to be published on July 20]], says Education Minister
headline: SSC results to be published on July 20, says Education Minister
summary: Education Minister Milon announced the date for SSC results and revealed plans for a unified question paper for both SSC and HSC exams.
details: Education Minister Milon has announced that the results of the Secondary School Certificate (SSC) examinations will be published on July 20.
The announcement was made during a press briefing where the minister discussed upcoming changes to the national examination system.
Minister Milon revealed a plan to introduce a 'one country, one question paper' system for both SSC and HSC examinations to ensure uniformity across the board.
This move is intended to standardize the assessment process and reduce discrepancies in grading across different education boards in Bangladesh.
caption:
Mark your calendars! SSC results are coming on July 20.

Education Minister Milon has announced that the results of the Secondary School Certificate (SSC) examinations will be published on July 20.

The announcement was made during a press briefing where the minister discussed upcoming changes to the national examination system.

Minister Milon revealed a plan to introduce a 'one country, one question paper' system for both SSC and HSC examinations to ensure uniformity across the board.

This move is intended to standardize the assessment process and reduce discrepancies in grading across different education boards in Bangladesh.
